text.0: Article on Ishmael: Written about religions, and he is a fool who spoke even against our perfect religion, by the great rabbi, our master Solomon ben Abraham ibn Aderet, of blessed memory. I saw a fool who is wise in his own eyes, an Ishmaelite, who was misled by his own vision and blinded by his own ignorance to speak even against our sacred book, the Torah of Moses, our master, peace be upon him. This contemptible and despicable man utters gibberish, responding to matters he does not comprehend. The beginning of his folly is his claim that he found disgrace in what was attributed to Judah regarding his relations with his daughter-in-law, and to Reuben regarding his relations with the mother of his brothers Dan and Naphtali. These are his words. And although it is not fitting to answer a fool according to his folly, especially regarding a matter whose answer is evident to all people, even to children, nevertheless, I will respond to him so that he may not consider himself wise and mislead others after him. The truth will guide the way. I say that these matters, like all others that may seem inappropriate to those who argue against our Torah, are actually proof of its authenticity. Particularly, the fact that the great sins of the people are revealed and recorded strengthens, in the eyes of any person with intelligence, the veracity of our Torah and all that is written in it, including miracles and signs, and our closeness to the Almighty. Let any person with understanding consider whether there exists any nation, many or few, that records in a book its great sins and transgressions so that they will be remembered for generations to come, to be accused and condemned. And if they did write such things willingly, without coercion, it is inconceivable that any human being with reason would tolerate such a thing. Now behold the sin that has been magnified beyond measure due to deviation from truth and propriety—the matter of the golden calf, as well as the affair of the spies and their defiance of the words of Moses, our master, peace be upon him, until their punishment came upon them, causing their corpses to fall in the wilderness. This is written in our book. And many such matters exist. All of these and everything in the Torah bear true testimony to our sacred book—it is true, nothing has been added to it nor removed, whether it concerns rebellion or greatness. Everything, even the smallest detail, has been recorded truthfully. Now consider another wonder: though many individuals and nations oppose our faith, none among them has ever claimed that our leaders, kings, and those of noble character were not human in form. All religious scholars have affirmed that the entire Torah was received by Moses, our master, peace be upon him, from the Almighty at Sinai and was given to the people of Israel. We have never heard of a single religious scholar who disputed this or denied these fundamental principles. Even the Christians and the Ishmaelites agree on this without objection. And now, human being, open your eyes and see: if this was written in the book by Moses, our master, peace be upon him, then it is the truth. And if it was added afterwards, how did our King David and all the kings from his lineage tolerate the recording of such matters in a book that specifies that he was born of an illicit union, and why did they not erase it? Furthermore, why would they tolerate a record in their book stating that his mother, who came from Moab, descended from an act of incest when the mother of the family engaged in relations with Lot, her father? And that his grandmother was an Ammonite? Could any rational person accept this unless it was written by divine command through His prophet, peace be upon him? And if someone claims that all of this was added to the book, as well as everything else of this nature in the Torah after the destruction, then let every sensible person, anyone with a brain in their head, consider: could all the books in the possession of Jews from the east, west, north, and south be gathered, altered in the same manner, and none of them remain unaltered in any word or passage? Who could have done such a thing—who, hating the Jewish nation and wishing to corrupt the religion, could have collected all the books without missing a single one and altered them all, including the books of the prophets and the writings, which also contain many such matters? All of this supposedly happened without a single scholar of any religion noticing? And if there had been a king, a ruler, an enemy of the Jews who gathered all the books and, by force, wrote and altered them, and all places feared him too much to remove what he wrote—this is nothing but the argument of a madman, a deranged fool with limitless foolishness. It is impossible that not a single copy would have survived in some corner of the world or in some hiding place. If all the kings and all the nations were to unite today to accomplish such a feat, they would not be able to. How much more so after such a long time? The Jews would have restored the distortions and removed the additions. And moreover, how is it possible that no one knows where and when this supposed madman who altered everything existed?
text.1: And behold, the Christians, who preceded the Ishmaelites who stray after their error, and who are our primary opponents in this faith, have scrutinized us thoroughly and left nothing unanswered. Undoubtedly, the Christians are far more knowledgeable in the holy scriptures—meaning the Torah and all of the Prophets and Writings—than the Ishmaelites. Now consider: even though the Christians preceded them, if they had found such corruption, and with their great community, if it had been known to them that any matter of this kind was recorded in the holy books, they would have certainly brought it to light. And how could this madman come now to corrupt the sacred books of truth, written by the ancients, who dedicated their entire lives to analysing letters and counting the verses of all the books, down to the minutest details such as full and defective spellings, written and spoken forms, and many other grammatical precisions that no religious scholar outside our people has ever reached? All this befits the Torah of truth, containing divine words spoken from the mouth of the Almighty, which were not written randomly. Likewise, the sages who received the Torah from Moses, our master, peace be upon him, transmitted it to their students and scrutinized all the commandments so that not a single unnecessary word was left in the Torah without meaning. This is evident to anyone who studies the books of the early sages in the commentaries on the Torah, which is arranged in the Talmud in our hands, passed down generation after generation until the Second Temple, and accepted back to the First Temple, to the prophets, to Joshua and the elders, and to Moses, our master, peace be upon him, who heard and received it from the Almighty at Sinai. And how can this madman, devoid of intelligence, attempt to introduce corruption into a sacred book, perfected with countless grammatical and textual refinements that no other nation or language has ever matched? This is nothing but blindness, bewilderment of heart, and a disease of the mind that has overtaken him.
text.2: The madman also said that he found something in the Book of Deuteronomy that, in his view, contains significant deviation and inconsistency, which none of his predecessors had noticed. He also claimed that he had posed this issue to many of our sages, and they were confused by it. His argument is as follows: In the Torah, in the fourth section of the second book, when recounting Moses' appointment as God's messenger to Pharaoh, the sons of Jacob and their offspring are listed. It states: "These are the names of the sons of Levi according to their families," mentioning Levi, son of Jacob, and his three sons: Gershon, Kehath, and Merari. Then, it lists the sons of Gershon and Merari. After that, it states that Kehath lived 130 years and names his four sons: Amram (who fathered Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them), Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. It then recounts that Aaron had four sons—Nadab, Avihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar—and a grandson, Pinchas. It also mentions that Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. Later, in the first section of the fourth book, when God commanded Moses, in the second month of the second year after the Exodus, to take a census of the Israelites, it recounts the number of Kehath's descendants. It states that the total number of Kehathites, from one month old and up, was 8,600, and that their leader was Elizaphan, son of Uzziel, son of Kehath, son of Levi, son of Jacob. When counting the Kehathites aged 30 to 50, there were 2,700 males. The madman then argues: "This is nonsense! How is it possible that Kehath had only four sons, and that those four had only seven male offspring, including Moses and Aaron, and that among them was also Elizaphan, their leader? Can any rational person believe this?" Thus speaks the madman.
text.3: And I say: In this, he praises himself, claiming that no one before him has noticed these supposed inconsistencies. He speaks the truth—no one before him has reached such depths of insanity! As for his claim that many of our sages were confused by his arguments—this is an outright lie, or he is deceiving himself, for he has never spoken with a true sage. I ask this madman: If you consider this to be an inconsistency, why did you not focus on even greater inconsistencies of this sort? If you have read this book, then you surely know that all the other tribes increased in number far beyond the tribe of Levi. And that although the forefathers listed in writing were few, their descendants, even among those explicitly mentioned, were much more numerous than those of Kehath. Do you not see that Reuben, son of Jacob, had only four sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi? And the Torah explicitly states that Pallu, one of the four, had only one son—Eliab. Eliab, in turn, had three sons: Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. And yet, despite this seemingly small number of ancestors, when the census was taken in the second year after the Exodus, the descendants of Reuben aged 20 and up numbered 46,500. Imagine how many they would have been if counted from one month old and up! Likewise, Judah, son of Jacob, had only three sons who continued his lineage: Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. Perez had two sons, Hezron and Hamul, yet the census of Judah’s descendants aged 20 and up counted 74,600. Had they been counted from one month old and up, their numbers would have been at least 200,000! So why does this not trouble you? According to your reasoning, this is even more implausible. But all of this stems from your confusion and deviation from the truth. Now, I will preface by saying that any rational person must recognize that it is impossible for anyone to alter a sacred text of the past, even if one of the ancient sages had composed it himself. No one can add to such a text unless there is a reason—either to strengthen faith or to enhance the honour of his nation by fabricating miracles. But without any benefit or purpose, no one, whether an individual or an entire nation, would add anything significant or trivial to a revered text. Especially in the case of our nation, which, with the agreement of all, received the Torah from Moses, our teacher, peace be upon him, through divine revelation. Could they have added numbers or genealogies that serve no purpose at all? If any alteration had been made, it would have been to their benefit—to enhance their prestige. Yet, if anything, the Torah states that they were few in number when they left Egypt, emphasizing the great miracle that a small people conquered the land of 31 kings. Indeed, as it is written about Gideon: "The people with you are too many for Me to give Midian into their hands, lest Israel boast and say, 'My own strength has saved me.'" And further: "The Lord said to Gideon, 'There are still too many people…'" until, finally, only 300 men remained, and God said: "With these 300, I will save you and give Midian into your hands."
text.4: Now, returning to the madman’s mistake: Even if we were to address his claim on its own terms—about the forefathers and their descendants—it is clear that the Torah does not list all the descendants, only a portion of them, specifically those who were the heads of family clans. Others, though numerous, were omitted from mention. For example, the Torah does not list all of Joseph’s descendants, only Manasseh and Ephraim, because they were the heads of their own tribes, as Jacob had prophesied. Similarly, in the case of Kehath, only those who were family heads were listed. Furthermore, Nadab and Avihu are mentioned even though they had no descendants because their story was essential to the Torah's narrative, as they died for offering unauthorized fire before the Lord. The Torah frequently organizes stories thematically rather than strictly chronologically. Moreover, the Torah does not mention Moses’ descendants here, even though it explicitly states elsewhere that he had two sons—Gershom and Eliezer—and that they produced many offspring, as written in Chronicles: "The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer. The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief. And the sons of Eliezer: Rehabiah the chief. And Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very numerous." This proves that the Torah did not mention all the sons of Kehath and likely omitted many of their offspring. Additionally, natural population growth is uneven. A father who has few children may have grandchildren who produce numerous offspring. Reuben, the eldest son of Jacob, had only four sons, while Dan had only one—Hushim. But Benjamin, the youngest of the brothers, had ten sons before descending to Egypt! Moreover, a man with many wives can father an extraordinary number of children. Ibzan had 30 sons and 30 daughters because he had many wives. Gideon had 70 sons. A single man can father a thousand children, as could have happened with Solomon, who had 700 wives and 300 concubines. Even today, among the Ishmaelite kings and their nobles, it is common to have an enormous number of offspring. So what is astonishing about the idea that Kehath's descendants multiplied greatly? There is no deviation from probability here—except in the mind of someone predisposed to denial and falsehood. Ultimately, only someone whose heart has turned toward deceit and heresy against Moses, our teacher, would call this a contradiction. And even if this were an extremely rare occurrence, rare events do happen. And if you deny this despite the evidence and numerous witnesses, then you have placed it in the realm of impossibility. And certainly, regarding the Almighty, if He wills to multiply a people or a family, nothing can stop Him. Only one who denies all faith would dispute this.
